text: Prior research on human detection of AI-generated content provides some baseline evidence relevant to H1, H3, and H5. Köbis et al. (2021) found that participants in a pre-registered experiment could not reliably detect deepfake audio-visual content, yet significantly overestimated their own detection ability, suggesting a gap between actual accuracy and confidence that interventions might target. On the broader question of trust in online information (H4), Dan et al. (2021) reviewed how visual mis- and disinformation on social media erodes public trust in democratic institutions, and Capraro et al. (2024) noted that generative AI has the potential to both exacerbate and ameliorate existing information-integrity challenges. Regarding attitudes toward AI (H2), Dwivedi et al. (2023) offered a multidisciplinary overview of how generative conversational AI is perceived across research, practice, and policy contexts, though they did not report experimental findings on attitude change. The retrieved list is otherwise thin on direct experimental evidence for the specific intervention effects hypothesized here.
